items.q: Overall gain is set too low. What does the image show?
o: Dark image with missing tissue detail
items.exp: Gain scales all echoes together, so low gain darkens tissue and hides real borders. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on gain.

items.q: The far field is dark while the near field looks right. Which control fixes it?
o: Raise the far time gain sliders
items.exp: Sound fades with depth, so far time gain restores distant brightness without flooding the near field. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on time gain compensation.

items.q: The near field is glaringly bright while the far field looks right. Which control fixes it?
o: Lower the near time gain sliders
items.exp: Near echoes need little boost, so turning down near sliders balances the image through depth. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on time gain compensation.

items.q: The heart fills only half the sector height. What should be changed?
o: Reduce depth so the heart fills the screen
items.exp: Right depth frames the heart large with fewer wasted lines, which lifts size and frame rate together. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on depth.

items.q: Where should the focal zone sit for a mitral valve study?
items.exp: Lateral detail is sharpest at the focus, so placing it at the target gives the crispest leaflets. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on focus.

items.q: What does raising transmit frequency do?
items.exp: Short waves resolve fine detail but fade fast, so high frequency suits shallow targets and low reaches deep. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on frequency choice.

items.q: Which probe best images an adult abdomen in FAST?
items.exp: Deep windows need penetration and a wide near view, which the low frequency curved probe gives. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on probe choice.

items.q: What does harmonic imaging improve?
o: Endocardial border definition with less near clutter
items.exp: Harmonics build from tissue itself and skip weak clutter, so borders stand out with a cleaner cavity. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on harmonic imaging.

items.q: Narrowing the sector width does what?
o: Raises frame rate for fast motion
items.exp: Fewer lines per frame means faster frames, so a tight sector tracks rapid wall motion smoothly. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on sector width and frame rate.

items.q: Fast wall motion looks jerky. What helps most?
o: Narrow the sector to raise frame rate
items.exp: Jerky motion means too few frames per beat, so fewer lines per frame restores smooth tracking. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on temporal resolution.

items.q: What does dynamic range compression change?
o: The shades of grey between black and white
items.exp: Compression maps echo strength to grey steps, so low values look contrasty and high values look smooth. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on dynamic range.

items.q: Write zoom differs from read zoom in what way?
o: Write zoom rescans the region with denser lines
items.exp: Write zoom acquires the boxed region afresh with tight line spacing, so detail is real rather than stretched pixels. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on zoom.

items.q: Colour box is large and the frame rate has fallen. What helps?
o: Shrink the colour box to the region of interest
items.exp: Colour costs lines, so a small box over the valve restores speed without losing the jet. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on colour box size.

items.q: Colour gain is too high. What is seen?
o: Colour bleeding over tissue outside flow
items.exp: Excess gain paints noise as flow, so gain is lowered until speckle just clears from tissue. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on colour gain.

items.q: The spectral trace looks pale and thin. What helps?
o: Raise spectral gain until the envelope is bright but clean
items.exp: Weak gain starves the envelope, so raising it reveals the true peak without blooming the edges. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on spectral gain.

items.q: Rib shadow crosses the sector. What is the best move?
items.exp: Bone blocks sound fully, so no knob recovers the hidden strip and the window must move. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on acoustic windows.

items.q: Lung covers the apex in a breathless patient. What helps?
o: Scan in end expiration or from another window
items.exp: Air scatters sound, so expiry shrinks lung cover or another window avoids it. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on acoustic windows.

items.q: Endocardium is unclear in a technically difficult patient. What is the next step?
o: Optimise harmonics, focus and gain before calling the study limited
items.exp: Many poor images recover with systematic knobs, so optimisation comes before labelling views unseen. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on image optimisation order.

items.q: Why does high frequency suit the apex in a slim patient but fail in a large patient?
o: Detail is excellent shallow but fades before deep targets
items.exp: Short waves resolve well yet attenuate fast, so depth and body size decide the trade. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on frequency choice.

items.q: Multiple focal zones sharpen the whole image but slow the frame. Why?
o: Each zone adds a scan pass per frame
items.exp: Several passes per line stack detail through depth at the cost of slower frames, so one zone at target often suffices. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on focus.

items.q: The image looks overly smooth with lost texture. What was changed?
o: Dynamic range set too high or smoothing set too strong
items.exp: Heavy smoothing erases speckle texture with borders, so easing it restores true tissue detail. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on post processing.

items.q: Cine loop review helps measurement because it does what?
o: Lets frames be stepped to true end systole and diastole
items.exp: Stepping finds exact timing frames that live motion blurs past, so volumes and Doppler align correctly. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on cine and ECG timing.

items.q: Why is ECG gating on during measurement?
o: It marks end diastole and end systole for consistent timing
items.exp: QRS and T landmarks time the frames, so beats compare fairly instead of drifting. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on ECG timing.

items.q: Depth is set far too deep for a parasternal view. What else suffers besides size?
items.exp: Wasted depth spends lines and widens spacing, so speed and detail both fall with the small image. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on depth.

items.q: Focus is left at maximum depth for an anterior structure. What is seen?
o: Blurred near target with sharp far field
items.exp: Detail peaks at the focus, so a far focus blurs the near target under study. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on focus.

items.q: Sector is opened very wide for a small heart. What is the effect?
o: Slower frames with more side clutter
items.exp: Wide sectors spend lines on empty space, so speed falls and side echoes rise for no gain. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on sector width.

items.q: Tissue looks grainy with speckle everywhere after raising gain. What is the fix?
o: Lower gain until blood is dark and muscle is mid grey
items.exp: Blood should read dark with muscle mid grey, so gain is set to that reference before judging pathology. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on gain reference.

items.q: Harmonics reduce frame rate slightly. When is that trade accepted?
o: When borders are unclear and detail matters more than speed
items.exp: Clean borders beat raw speed for volumes and wall calls, so harmonics stay on unless motion needs speed. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on harmonic imaging.

items.q: A trainee raises overall gain to fix a dark far field. What is the better lesson?
o: Use far time gain so the near field is not flooded
items.exp: Overall gain lifts all depths together, so depth selective sliders correct fading without near bloom. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on time gain compensation.

items.q: Colour jet looks small with a high scale setting. What should be tried?
o: Lower the scale toward the expected velocity
items.exp: An over high ceiling shrinks jets, so matching scale to flow shows true jet size before grading. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on colour scale.

items.q: Why save stills and loops rather than trusting memory?
o: Saved images allow review, audit and comparison
items.exp: Stored frames can be measured and rechecked, so reporting rests on evidence rather than recall. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on documentation.

items.q: The ECG trace on screen is noisy. What should be checked first?
items.exp: Timing marks need clean ECG, so skin contact and leads are fixed before measuring. Guideline: BSE minimum dataset, section on ECG timing.
